thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — runtime pod crashloop on gpu-node-12. Error pattern: CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address. Affected service: inference-runtime, model: redwood-open-3b (v2.3). Detected 2026-03-15T18:12:03Z. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1764501123 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: paging @mira (oncall) — escalation to infra SRE if not acked in 2m :bell:

mira: taking it. reading logs now.

mira: quick snapshot — 6 pods on node gpu-node-12 in CrashLoopBackOff, kube shows OOM + GPU error. Not seeing obvious kernel OOM only CUDA faults in container logs.

samir: can you paste the last 50 lines from one of the crashing pods? also need `dmesg` from the node and `nvidia-smi` output.

mira: paste logs from runtime pod (id runtime-7f8c9):

```
I0315 18:11:58.123456 1 server.cpp:345] starting inference loop
E0315 18:12:01.987654 1 cuda_executor.cpp:512] CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
E0315 18:12:01.987660 1 cuda_executor.cpp:513] address: 0x7f9c2a3f8   kernel: attention_kernel.cu:142
E0315 18:12:01.987662 1 runtime.cpp:210] runtime panic: CUDA illegal memory access, aborting
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

mira: node dmesg shows NVRM Xid messages:

```
[   34.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=24567, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[   34.123460] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000010, intr 10000000.
```

lucas: +1 those Xid errors. Looks like GPU fault, could be driver, kernel, or a model kernel race. Any recent runtime build or kernel changes?

mira: rollout yesterday of runtime v2.3 (commit abc123). Kernel on node is 5.17.12, NVIDIA driver 535.86. Let me note that.

anya: FYI support queue — customer "Acadia Health" reporting inference failures and timeouts starting ~18:12 UTC. Emily opened a ticket.

emily: ticket #7832 linked https://support.redwood/7832 — they see 503s and partial streaming frames. Customer impact: 2 production projects down.

samir: immediate mitigation options we can do now: 1) cordon + drain gpu-node-12 to move other pods off, 2) route traffic away from replicas with the GPU affinity (use routing policy to fallback to cpu-quantized variant), 3) rollback runtime to previous build (v2.2) which had no reports.

mira: starting 1 & 2 now — cordon/drain and reroute. samir can you prepare rollback if needed.

lucas: running drain:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

lucas: drain in progress — pods are rescheduling. cluster autoscaler kicking to spin up additional GPU nodes to accommodate reschedules.

ops-bot: live metrics: 8% of inference traffic currently hitting fallback (cpu-quantized) policy. Error rate for inference-runtime increased to 12% in last 5m.

mira: routing rule applied: route 100% new traffic for model redwood-open-3b to fallback cpu-quant-1 for affected orgs, leaving canary on GPUs disabled.

samir: preparing rollback patch for runtime — building v2.2 image. If we roll back, we need to coordinate canary and ensure current in-flight requests drained.

mira: also spinning up remote memcheck and collecting GPU crash dump. Commands I'm running on node (sharing):
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80 > /tmp/dmesg-xid.txt
sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --exclude-logs --output-file /tmp/nvreport.tar.gz
kubectl exec -n infra debug-pod -- /bin/bash -c "ls -l /var/crash || true"
```

samir: good. while that's running, quick check — any pattern by model sequence length or batching? lucas can you dump recent request traces?

lucas: pulling traces from tracing service — see repeated requests with long prefix length ~2048 tokens and batch sizes of 16 hitting those GPUs. That may exacerbate kernel memory usage.

mira: mitigation additional: temporarily reduce max_batch_size to 8 for GPU pools and set a per-request token cap to 1024. Applying policy change now.

ops-bot: policy update applied: inference-runtime GPU batch_size max = 8, token_max = 1024 for redwood-open-3b on GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu.

emily: updated customer ticket with mitigation steps and ETA; told Acadia Health that we routed to fallback and are investigating GPU faults.

samir: nvbug report uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1764501123/nvreport.tar.gz. I'll run `cuda-memcheck` on a reproducer once we have a core dump.

lucas: after draining node, new pods started on other GPUs and I see success logs — 200 responses resumed for most traffic. Error rate dropped to 1.6%.

mira: at 18:34 UTC I'm handing off to @samir for deep debug and root cause analysis. I'm available if you need immediate help.

samir: ack taking it for 2 hours. immediate next steps: collect coredumps, capture NVidia driver stack traces (nvidia-smi dmon), run small reproducer with sanitized model weights under cuda-memcheck and ASAN for host paths. Also capture runtime commit id and revert if reproducer fails.

samir: starting rollback to v2.2 on a canary subset while we reproduce — executing rollout: `kubectl set image deploy/inference-runtime inference-runtime=registry.redwood/re-runtime:v2.2`

ops-bot: deploy bot: Rollout started for deployment inference-runtime in namespace inference. Canary size = 5%.

samir: canary looks healthy after 3m. Increasing to 25%.

lucas: confirm driver/kernel versions on new nodes match original, so less likely a wide driver regression. Might be a runtime scheduling/kernel optimization in v2.3 that triggered a race under large batches.

samir: reproducer under cuda-memcheck failed to show illegal access immediately but we captured a coredump from one of the crashed pods. Uploading to s3 and kicking off symbolicated analysis job.

mira: customer impact summary so far: two customers experienced increased errors and partial unavailability for ~22 minutes (18:12–18:34) until routing to fallback. No data exfiltration. Billing unaffected.

anya: flagged for post-incident review with product + infra — priority: model rollback safety nets, default lower batch sizes, better runbook for Xid errors.

samir: initial mitigation result: roll back to v2.2 for fleet (completed), error rate returned to baseline ~0.2% across last 15m. I'm keeping node gpu-node-12 quarantined for deeper hardware checks.

ops-bot: Incident created: https://redwood.incidents/1764501123 — sev: P1 — status: Mitigated.

mira: marking incident as mitigated. handing off to samir for postmortem and RCA. I'll close oncall shift in 10m.

samir: I'll run thorough kernel and runtime bisect tomorrow; collecting all artifacts: nvreport, coredump, runtime logs, tracers, dmesg, nodetool output, and will propose fix (either runtime patch to fix kernel op or suggest safety guard in serving runtime to catch illegal access and fall back early).

emily: customers notified with summary and ETA for RCA.

mira: thanks team. incident resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

(automated note) incident-bot: resolution recorded: mitigated at 2026-03-15T18:34:40Z. Total customer impact window ~22 minutes. Follow-up owner: samir for RCA.
